completion:
Clearly identify the product.
3. Record the testing procedures.
4. Define advertised specifications.
5. Detail initial observations (e.g., appearance, labeling).
6. Document any setup instructions followed.
7. Perform tests based on industry standards or accepted testing methodologies.
8. Setting: Note the environment in which the tests are conducted.
9. Instruments: Use calibrated, accurate, and reliable testing instruments.
10. Record test results.
11. Compare test results with advertised specifications.
12. Highlight discrepancies.
13. Use quantitative data (e.g., measurements, times, efficiencies).

17. Summarize the overall findings.
